svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Where the picture sits in a terminal window
svg.desc: A terminal window with the character picture centred in it, the leftover rows split above and below, every row padded out to the full width, and the status line in reverse video on the last row. Beside it, why padding replaces clearing and why colour is written as runs.
svg.text: Where the picture sits, and why nothing is ever cleared
The window is almost never the grid's shape. What is left over is split, and every row is padded out to the full width.
one terminal window
scheme grey ramp coarse 15.0fps 80x30 s r i +
the remainder is split above and below, so the picture is centred
the amber line is where every row is padded out to: the last frame
is overwritten rather than cleared
the status line is reserved first, which is why the canvas is one row short - and it is
drawn in reverse video, which works on a terminal with no colours at all
padded, not cleared
##%%@@%%## the last frame
the amber part is padding, and it costs the same
as clearing and redrawing - without the flash
fill mode is the exception. Letterboxing leaves cells
the picture stops writing to, so it forces a real clear.
colour written as runs
three calls rather than 250: adjacent cells of one
colour are written together
a greyscale row goes as a single string, because
greyscale passes None rather than a uniform array -
not a missing value, but the cheapest instruction
there is: draw in the terminal's own foreground
curses owns the screen
Anything written to standard
output or standard error while
curses holds the terminal
corrupts the picture until the
next full repaint.
So both are redirected to a log
file before any of this starts,
and one thread does all of the
drawing - curses is not safe to
drive from two.
A resize arrives as a keypress
rather than as an event, so a
resize and a keystroke cannot
race: they are one queue.
None of this runs in the
enclosure, which boots with
--no-terminal and has no
monitor to run it on.
